ns2:course.label: Making and Meaning
ns2:course.description: Introduction to the relationship of material, method, and process to meaning in art practice. Through research, critique, and application of concepts in material studio processes, students will explore a diverse range of methods of achieving meaning in an artwork. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 hours. Prerequisite: ARTS 102 and ARTS 104.
ns2:course.courseSectionInformation: May be repeated to a maximum of 6 hours. Prerequisite: ARTS 102 and ARTS 104.
ns2:course.sectionRegistrationNotes: Restricted to Graphic Design or Crafts or History of Art or Photography or Industrial Design or Painting or Sculpture or Art Education or New Media major(s).
ns2:course.classScheduleInformation: Class Materials Fee of $30 required. A student registered in one or more Art & Design course(s) exhibiting this message, will be assessed a $95 facility use fee once each term.
